summary.text: Cosmic inflation is a theory that space expanded exponentially fast in the very early universe.
The expansion supercooled the universe and ended when the energy of the field driving it condensed into hot, dense particles, a process called reheating.
Quantum fluctuations in a microscopic region were magnified to cosmic size and became the seeds for the growth of structure in the universe.

facts.label: Growth in size
facts.value: Radius grew from about 4 × 10⁻²⁹ m to about 0.9 m

facts.label: Hypothetical field
facts.value: The field thought to drive it is the inflaton

facts.label: Kavli Prize
facts.value: Starobinsky, Guth and Linde won it in 2014

items.prompt: Picture a hot, expanding cloud of matter spread perfectly smoothly. Why would stars struggle to form in it?

options.label: Hot clouds always turn into pure light before stars form
A uniform spread has no force to pull matter into clumps
Even clouds collapse too quickly to make separate stars
Expansion only acts on clouds that are unevenly dense

items.explain: Clumping needs density contrast, and a completely uniform density has no force to drive it.

items.prompt: Inflation stretched microscopic ripples to enormous size. What role did those ripples play afterward?

options.label: They were the particles that made up the first stars
They stopped the expansion once they grew big enough
They carried the energy that drove the expansion
They became the seeds for the growth of structure

items.explain: Quantum fluctuations magnified to cosmic size became the seeds for the growth of structure in the universe.

items.prompt: When inflation ended, what happened to the field that had been driving it?

options.label: Its energy condensed into hot, dense particles
It switched on a faster second round of expansion
It spread out evenly until nothing was left of it
It was captured by stars forming in the universe

items.explain: Inflation ended when the energy of the driving field condensed into hot, dense particles, called reheating.

items.prompt: Observations show the universe is flat to within a few percent, and expansion makes the universe flatter over time. What does that imply about the early universe?

options.label: It must have been strongly curved at first
Its flatness then was a matter of chance
It must have been exceptionally close to flat
It could not be compared with the present universe

items.explain: Because expansion increases flatness, the early universe must have been exceptionally close to flat.

items.prompt: Particle theories predict heavy magnetic charges should dominate the universe, yet none are found. How could inflation account for that?

options.label: Inflation would destroy each one when it ended
Expansion would spread them apart, lowering their density
Inflation would turn them into ordinary particles
Expansion would pack them together out of view

items.explain: A period of inflation below the temperature where monopoles form would separate them as the universe expands, lowering their observed density.

items.prompt: A physicist claims we know exactly which particle-physics process drove inflation, and that every scientist accepts the theory. What is wrong?

options.label: The detailed mechanism is unknown, and some scientists dissent
No observation has ever matched anything the theory predicts
The theory says inflation lasted exactly 10⁻³⁵ seconds
The theory was only proposed after the year 2000

items.explain: The detailed particle physics mechanism is unknown, and some scientists dissent from the view that observations support inflation.
